units.translation: But it is not possible for me either to be silent or not to be silent about these fortunes.
What profit is there for me to live, but why did I not quickly throw myself—?
BA. We will not give you up to the snatchings of winged creatures. CH. But if to the more hateful of hostile serpents.
But let us leave these things,
But she—the mother of the king—is rushing.
But in my opinion you will soon know—.
But since it seems good to do these things
But throw the arm-straps around your sides.
But, O wretched one, let go of the anger you have.
But may you abound with good things in return for good things.
But if these things seem good to you, let someone loosen the sandals under your feet
But may it not happen somehow.
But how might we share safe counsels (thus Porson for κοινωσώμεθ᾽ ἄν πως)?
But, O great Fates, may it end here by the will of Zeus.
I would not exchange my misfortune for your servitude.
by hands that slay one another
There are no examples of the dual number in Aeschylus, who used only the plural number.
And strife was stirred up among them.
These two, as I seemed to see, were making strife between themselves (thus Blomfield for ἀλλήλησι).
What enmities and affections and gatherings are there towards one another.
Winds showing opposing strife against one another.
The earth has drunk blood by murder at the hands of one another.
And there was no aid for one another.
And they fell upon one another.
For Thracian blasts were shattering the ships against one another (thus Triclinius for ἀλλήλησι).
If then you relax for those who kill one another.
Ares, both civil and bold against one another.
by a wave of foreign men
And one torch rises to heaven from one place, another from another.
One from one place, another from another, they raised a cry throughout the city.
And he will learn from one and another.
Everyone is ready to utter blame against foreigners.
